learning_outcomes.text: Approach the reality of underdevelopment and marginalization.

Acquire a global and supportive vision of reality, complementing conventional technical education to achieve comprehensive training that includes the ethical principles that should govern professional practice.
Acquire specific professional training in the field of technological cooperation and development.
Participate in a debate forum on technical cooperation and development at the University of Oviedo.
Students with a greater critical sense, respect for diversity and capacity for participation in social activities.
Approach the reality of underdevelopment and marginalization.

Acquire a global and supportive vision of reality, complementing conventional technical education to provide students with comprehensive training that includes the ethical principles that should govern their professional practice.
Acquire specific professional training in the field of technological cooperation and development.
Participate in a debate forum on technical cooperation and development at the University of Oviedo.
Put into practice critical thinking, respect for diversity and the ability to participate in social activities.

syllabus_topics: Cooperation for development: methods and agents.
Infrastructure, construction and materials technologies in cooperation for development.
Energy technologies in cooperation for development.
Cooperation for development projects based on energy supply to rural communities and other disadvantaged groups.
Information technologies in cooperation for development.
Digital policy: digital divides; biases in design and use; new rights and properties; ICT as agents of change and social control.
Environmental technologies in cooperation for development.
Atmospheric pollution: impacts of climate change.
teaching_methods: Group work simulating volunteer teams of technological NGOs
Project work as part of a real awareness campaign

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (EX_FIN) - report and verbal presentation on a group project
Evaluated practice 1 (P1) - application of Topic 1 contents
Evaluated practice 2 (P2) - application of Topic 2 contents
Evaluated practice 3 (P3) - application of Topic 3 contents
Evaluated practice 4 (P4) - application of Topic 4 contents
Evaluated practice 5 (P5) - application of Topic 5 contents
Evaluated practice 6 (P6) - application of Topic 6 contents

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 75% attendance (44 hours) is required to be evaluated; otherwise, the grade will be 'No Presentado'. The final grade is calculated as: FINAL GRADE = EX_FIN x 0.3 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1 + A x 0.05 + PA x 0.05. A minimum of 5 points from this formula is needed to pass. For extraordinary calls, students must notify the faculty at least 4 weeks before the exam date to receive project and practice assignments, and submit reports at least 48 hours before the exam. The final grade is calculated as: FINAL GRADE = EX_EXTRA x 0.4 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1, with a minimum of 5 points required to pass.
